cap: In the male pelvis the ductus deferens crosses over the ureter, widens into an ampulla and joins the seminal vesicle to form the ejaculatory duct, which opens on the seminal colliculus of the prostatic urethra. Peritoneum dips only to the rectovesical pouch; Denonvilliers fascia lies between the prostate and rectum, so a digital rectal exam feels the posterior prostate. During emission the internal urethral sphincter closes; if it fails, semen flows back into the bladder.
